page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is an x86_64 Cloud Compute server featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.0 GHz. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and is equipped with 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU architecture supports AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA instructions, with a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tiers. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the server in the bottom 25%, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores rank in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks achieves average performance at 367.64 GB/sec, but drops to the bottom 25% for larger uncached blocks. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also reflect lower-tier performance, with Redis handling 2.63 million operations per second.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest performance profile, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or sustained high-performance compute. It is suited for basic web serving, lightweight application hosting, development environments, and small-scale testing. The inclusion of 160 GB of NVMe SSD storage provides fast local storage access, making it a viable choice for budget-conscious deployments requiring moderate storage capacity but minimal processing overhead.
description: The Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is a shared-CPU Cloud Compute server featuring 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor at 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmark results position this instance in the lower performance tiers, with stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench scores falling in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. While its cached memory bandwidth performs at an average level, uncached memory operations and database performance are relatively weak. This server is a cost-effective option for non-critical, low-intensity workloads such as development environments, basic web serving, and lightweight application hosting where dedicated CPU resources are not required.
